verdict: The four scripts implement their specs closely and all 106 tests run clean (93 pass, 13 needs-app skips). Of 40 mutations, 31 were caught. One measure is computed wrongly by design: throughput per active hour treats every ledger silence over 10 min as idle time, and a working session writes no ledger lines. Two statistics are biased: the pooled plant counts and coverage that counts superseded cards. Two blinding weaknesses: seed sentences are a fixed template, and no audit sees what the checker helper reads. The rest are test gaps where a mechanism-removing mutation survived: the in-lock epoch and ce checks, the seed shuffle, the TURN-END last-line rule, the commit-record sha and the S1 window check.

tests.command: node tools/lane.mjs --label review-U4 --timeout-s 300 -- node --test --test-concurrency=1 tcb/test/render.test.mjs tcb/test/audit.test.mjs tcb/test/seed.test.mjs tcb/test/check-queue.test.mjs

findings.claim: time.active_s and throughput_per_h treat every gap over sleep_gap_ms between consecutive ledger lines as quiet time. During a step no script writes a ledger line (no heartbeat kind in CONTRACT 3.7; the watcher writes only event lines), so the session's working hours are subtracted as 'quiet'. throughput_per_h then comes out far too high, or null.
findings.evidence: By hand: a bind line at 10:00, intake at 11:00:00, commit at 11:00:05, 3 ids covered, sleep_gap 600000. The gap 10:00 to 11:00 (3600 s) is quiet, so wall_s is 3605, active_s 5 and throughput_per_h = 3/(5/3600) = 2160. With only bind and commit 2 h apart, active_s is 0 and throughput is null. T15 passes only because its fixture puts ledger lines less than 10 min apart.
findings.fix: Divide throughput by wall_s hours and keep quiet_gaps and active_s as readings. Better: take activity gaps from the model-call timestamps of the task's own transcripts (parsed already in loadSession), not from ledger lines.

findings.claim: plants pooling sums k, found and contra_found over every stored x_ certificate, so a review that was re-certified after a STALE certificate counts two or three times. contra_k counts the against-hope plants of every sealed/plants/<task>.json, including tasks that have no certificate yet. The numerator and denominator cover different sets, and the Clopper-Pearson bounds are too narrow.
findings.evidence: Two certificates for one review, each {k:3, found:3}, pool to k 6 / found 6 instead of 3/3. With plants for tasks A and B, each with one against-hope plant, and only A certified with contra_found 1, contra_rate = 1/2 instead of 1/1.
findings.fix: Pool one certificate per task: the latest, or the VALID one per tms labels. Take contra_k only from the sealed/plants files of the tasks in that set.

findings.claim: In freeze and post-review batches every seed item carries the same synthetic sentence: sid 's1' and the fixed text 'Using X, the measured Y was V U under the conditions stated for the source.', with applies_to equal to the card's full conditions. Real items carry their authored sentence. One checker sees up to 7 template sentences beside real prose and can tell the seeds apart, which breaks R42/R43 ('cannot tell a seed from a real item'). The spec names a template, but the design rule it serves is defeated.
findings.evidence: syntheticSentence() returns a constant shape. check-queue gives every seed in a sentence mode a sentence (withSentence = mode !== 'intake'), and T6 checks key sets only, not text shape.
findings.fix: Build each seed's sentence from a real fact sentence of the same committed object (its text, sid style and applies_to), changing only what the operator needs. Or draw the template from several phrasings with rng and use sids absent from the real sentences. Add a test that no sentence text is shared by all seed items.

findings.claim: The coordinator form never checks helper reads. udi_reads looks at main only, and no read_prefixes are applied to helpers. The checker runs as a coordinator helper (check-queue spec: 'The coordinator, never a child, starts the checker'), so a checker that reads sealed/seeds/<b>.json (the key) or a second queue batch is never flagged. CONTRACT 3.21 says 'audit flags a checker that read more than one batch'. The task form's {batch} expansion also allows every batch.
findings.evidence: readsOf(main) only at line 458. There is no helper read loop in coordinatorForm. In taskForm, {batch} is expanded to all batchDirs (235) with no count of distinct batches read.
findings.fix: In the coordinator form, for each helper transcript of agent type checker, apply tcb/profiles/checker.json read_prefixes with {batch} bound to the batch it read first. List any other read (sealed/, a second queue/<b>/) in a checker_reads field, and exit 1 when that list is not empty.

findings.claim: isExcludedCard treats only 'rejected' and 'superseded' as untrusted. Cards labelled 'pending' or 'unverifiable' are not trusted under R24 ('witnessed or confirmed cards'), yet they render in the main pack body and enter synthesis rows. Their measured.effect counts toward the effects column and can set 'weak: disagreement' when no trusted card disagrees.
findings.evidence: In a synthesis row, a confirmed card with effect improves plus a pending card with effect worsens gives effects [improves, worsens] and weak: true. R24 says synthesis reads only trusted items.
findings.fix: Exclude every card whose label is not witnessed or confirmed (isExcludedCard = !['witnessed','confirmed'].includes(cardLabel(id))). Keep the sentence labels (PENDING/STALE) visible as the spec asks.

findings.claim: With f5_given true, isCounted looks only at the last status. A card labelled 'superseded' (a confirmed correction replaced it; under R16 that overrides every status) whose own last status is still 'confirmed' or 'witnessed' is counted for covered ids, held-out recall, Chapman and throughput. The f5-false branch does exclude superseded cards.
findings.evidence: Card A (confirmed) superseded by card B (confirmed): both count, so a wrong card raises recall and Chapman n1/n2 and inflates m.
findings.fix: Add && cardLabel(id) !== 'superseded' to the f5 branch.

findings.claim: Removing the shuffle (const order = all) passes every test. Seeds then always sit after the real items in batch.json, which breaks R42's 'random position'.
findings.evidence: Mutation C3 left 22 pass, 0 fail. T5 compares the arrays of item ids, which differ anyway because the seed contents (and so seed ids) change with the rng.
findings.fix: In T5, assert that the seed items' positions in batch.json differ between rng seeds, and that across a few seeds a seed position is not always after every real item.

findings.claim: Removing the epoch re-check inside the lock (await recheck(h)) passes every test. A fence that lands between the pre-lock check and the lock would let a stale attempt's audit lines be written.
findings.evidence: Mutation A1 left 20 pass, 0 fail. T15 only exercises the pre-lock compare at line 180.
findings.fix: Add a test that raises the row's epoch while a test-held lock blocks the script, for example a sleeper the test spawns and releases. Expect 65 and no audit file.

findings.claim: Removing the --ce check inside the run lock passes all render and audit tests. CONTRACT 1.1 requires the compare inside the lock, and only the pre-lock check is exercised.
findings.evidence: Mutations R9 (26 pass) and A12 (20 pass).
findings.fix: Add one test per script that changes run/coord.json ce while the lock is held by a test-spawned holder, then releases it. Expect exit 64 and no write.

findings.claim: The R30 rule is that the last non-blank line is exactly TURN-END <field>. Weakening it to 'any line equals TURN-END <field>' passes every test, so a note after the TURN-END line is not exercised.
findings.evidence: Mutation A10 left 20 pass. T10's cases all end with or lack the line; none has text after it.
findings.fix: Add the case 'TURN-END f1\nextra note' to T10, expecting it to count as bad.

findings.claim: Removing the comparison of object bytes with the commit record's sha256 passes every test. T7 edits object bytes, which getObject's id check catches anyway, so an edited sha256 in the record is never tested.
findings.evidence: Mutation R1 left 26 pass. getObject compares only 16 hex of the name.
findings.fix: In T7, also edit an output's sha256 in store/commits/<t>.<step>.json and expect exit 3 object-mismatch.

findings.claim: Removing the S1 'redrawn until not in window' check passes every test. The tests' windows never contain a drawn quote, so the redraw branch is never run.
findings.fix: In T2, pass an rng stub whose first draw yields a 6-word quote placed in the window, and assert that the result differs from it.

mutations.what: R4 remove seed-id search in objects
R9 remove --ce check inside the lock
A1 remove epoch re-check inside the lock
A5 remove BOM strip (equivalent: String.trim strips U+FEFF)
A7 remove harvested regex (equivalent: isUnder(abs, F/staging/harvested) covers it)
A10 TURN-END any line instead of last line
A12 remove --ce check inside the lock
S2 unanswered seed counted detected (three-valued result collapsed)
S3 J4 followed no longer unqualifies
S4 S1 quote not checked against the window
C1 seed source may be a real item
C4 intake seed-id tamper check removed
C5 window not clamped at the end
C6 flagged sentence of a confirmed card not queued

notes: Scratch copy and per-mutation outputs: review-tmp/U4/ (orig/, tcb/, out-*.txt, mut.sh). The unit's files were not edited, and every copy was restored after its mutation.

No unsafe action was found in the unit: no kill, no network call, and no write outside the run root. Path segments come from validated row ids, the batch regex, or safeRelPath plus fixed_files. Transcript parsing happens before the lock in all four scripts.
Spec contradiction, not filed: audit T14 says W_star_coord 'value: null' gives 'the same calls_over as a reading', but a null value has no limit. The test uses gate:false instead.
